# VFD Pump Control Narrative: Template and Example (P-1102)

## How the template is built

- **Reference, don't copy.** Tags, ranges, engineering units, and alarm setpoints stay in the I/O list and alarm database. The narrative names the tag and the database row. It never restates the value, so the narrative cannot drift out of date when someone changes a setpoint.
- **Describe behavior, not data.** The narrative's job is to say what the pump does: when it can start, what stops it, what the operator sees, and how it fails.
- **Keep timers and logic parameters here.** Debounce times, ramp times, and restart delays usually don't live in either spreadsheet. They go in Section 9, unless your alarm database already holds them.
- **Write the standard once.** For 30 or more pumps, write the common VFD pump behavior once as a class description (Section 0). Each pump narrative then records only its specific devices and deviations. Reviews get faster and inconsistencies show up.

---

> Items marked **[TBC]** are my assumptions or details not given in the brief. Confirm them with the process engineer or client before Rev 0. They are also collected in Section 12.

### 0. Standard Class Reference
This module follows **VFD Pump Class Standard [doc no., rev]**.
☒ Deviations listed in sections: 5, 6 (process-specific permissives and interlocks)

### 1. Module Identification
| Item | Entry |

| P&ID / revision | [ ] |
| Unit / area | [ ] |

| Destination vessel | T-120 Hold Tank |
| Pump type | [TBC: centrifugal assumed] |
| Controller / I/O node | [ ] |
| VFD tag and network address | [VFD tag, e.g., VFD-1102] / [ ] |
| Hygienic / CIP duty | [TBC: see Open Item 3] |

### 2. Associated Devices
| Function | Tag | I/O List Ref | Alarm DB Ref | Fail-safe state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VFD run command | [P-1102 run cmd tag] | [ ] | n/a | De-energize = stop |
| VFD run feedback | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | |
| VFD fault | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | |
| VFD speed reference | [ ] | [ ] | n/a | |
| VFD speed feedback | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | |
| T-110 low level switch (dry-run protection) | LSL-110 | [ ] | [ ] | [TBC: contact open on low level and on wire break] |
| P-1102 discharge pressure | PT-1102 | [ ] | [ ] | Bad quality on out-of-range or wire break |
| T-120 high level switch (overfill protection) | LSH-120 | [ ] | [ ] | [TBC: contact open on high level and on wire break] |

### 3. Modes of Operation
| Mode | Command source | Speed reference source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Out of Service | None, start blocked | n/a | Used for maintenance |
| Manual (HMI) | Operator faceplate | Operator entry | All interlocks I1–I3 active |
| Auto (Batch) | Batch transfer phase [phase name, TBC] | Batch system | All interlocks I1–I3 active |
| Local (field) | [TBC: does a local HOA or VFD keypad control exist?] | [ ] | If yes, state whether PLC interlocks are bypassed in Local. See Open Item 4. |

Mode transfer: Auto → Manual is bumpless. The pump keeps running and holds the last speed reference. Manual → Auto hands control to the batch system, which must issue a start. [TBC]

### 4. Speed Control
- Reference units: % of maximum speed [TBC: confirm the batch system sends %, not flow EU]
- The reference is clamped to the minimum and maximum speed in the VFD parameter set. The minimum speed protects the pump and motor cooling.
- Ramps are VFD-internal. Values are in Section 9.
- Bad or out-of-range reference in Auto: the pump stops and raises an alarm. [TBC]

### 5. Start Permissives (DEVIATION: process-specific)
| # | Permissive | Tag | Bypassable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Module not Out of Service | — | No |
| P2 | No active VFD fault | VFD fault | No |
| P3 | No active interlock trip | — | No |
| P4 | T-110 level not low (pump has suction supply) | LSL-110 | [TBC: see Open Item 3, CIP] |
| P5 | T-120 level not high (destination can accept product) | LSH-120 | No |
| P6 | PT-1102 signal healthy (not bad quality) | PT-1102 | [TBC: supervisor bypass for instrument failure?] |
| P7 | [TBC: transfer path valves proven open, if any exist between T-110 and T-120] | [ ] | [ ] |

### 6. Interlocks (Trips) (DEVIATION: process-specific)
| # | Condition | Tag | Delay (Sec 9) | Action | Reset type | Bypassable? | Active in modes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | T-110 low level (dry-run protection) | LSL-110 | T_LSL110 | Stop pump | Auto-clear, new start required | [TBC: CIP] | Manual, Auto |
| I2 | T-120 high level (overfill protection) | LSH-120 | T_LSH120 | Stop pump | Auto-clear, new start required | No | Manual, Auto |
| I3 | Discharge pressure high (deadhead / blocked discharge) | PT-1102 | Per alarm DB | Stop pump | Manual reset | No | Manual, Auto |
| I4 | PT-1102 bad quality while running | PT-1102 | T_PT_BQ | [TBC: stop pump, or alarm only] | Manual reset | [TBC] | Manual, Auto |

Notes:
- I1 is the normal end-of-transfer condition, and the batch phase may expect it. The phase logic should normally stop the pump before LSL-110 trips. A trip on LSL-110 during a phase is reported to the batch system with reason code "Source Low." [TBC: confirm whether phase end is by level/weight or by LSL-110.]
- I2 protects T-120 from overfill. If an independent high-high or SIS function exists on T-120, reference it here: [SRS ref / n/a].
- I1–I3 are process interlocks, not safety instrumented functions. [TBC: confirm with the client HAZOP that LSH-120 has no SIL requirement.]

### 7. Alarms
| Alarm DB Ref | Tag | Description | Control action | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ ] | LSL-110 | T-110 low level | Interlock I1 | Check T-110 contents. If unexpected mid-transfer, check for leaks or an upstream issue. |
| [ ] | LSH-120 | T-120 high level | Interlock I2 | Check T-120 level and downstream draw-off. Do not restart until level is reduced. |
| [ ] | PT-1102 | Discharge pressure high | Interlock I3 | Check for a closed downstream valve or a blockage before resetting. |
| [ ] | PT-1102 | Discharge pressure low while running [TBC] | Alarm only | Possible loss of prime, air ingress, or line break. Inspect. |
| [ ] | PT-1102 | Signal bad quality | Interlock I4 / alarm [TBC] | Call instrument tech. |
| [ ] | P-1102 | Run feedback fail | Stop, latched | Check VFD and contactor. |
| [ ] | P-1102 | VFD fault | Stop | Read the fault code on the HMI or VFD and act on it. |
| [ ] | P-1102 | Batch comms loss | Stop | Notify control or batch support. |

### 8. Equipment Monitoring and Failure Handling
| Condition | Detection | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Run feedback fail | After T_FB_FAIL | Run command removed, alarm, latched until reset |
| Uncommanded run | After T_FB_FAIL | Alarm |
| VFD fault | Fault bit over network / hardwired | Stop, alarm. VFD auto-reset disabled [TBC]. |
| VFD network comms loss | Network status | Stop (VFD comms-loss action set to stop), alarm |
| Batch comms loss (Auto) | Batch watchdog | Stop, alarm. Mode stays Auto. Restart requires a batch command. [TBC] |
| PT-1102 bad quality | Out-of-range / channel fault | See I4 and P6 |
| LSL-110 or LSH-120 wire break | Fail-safe wiring reads as alarm state | The pump stops or cannot start (fails safe). Tech checks the switch. |
| Power restoration | — | Pump stays stopped in all modes |
| PLC restart / download | — | Pump stays stopped. Mode retained [TBC]. |

### 9. Module Parameters
| Parameter | Value | Units | HMI adjustable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T_FB_FAIL | [TBC] | s | No | Per class standard |
| Ramp up / down | [TBC] | s | No | VFD parameter. Check for water hammer on stop. |
| T_LSL110 (I1 debounce) | [TBC] | s | No | Keep short. The pump is running dry during this time. Allow for vortex or splash at low level. |
| T_LSH120 (I2 debounce) | [TBC] | s | No | Keep short. Overfill risk. |
| T_PT_BQ | [TBC] | s | No | |
| Low-pressure alarm arming delay after start | [TBC] | s | No | Prevents nuisance alarms while the pump is ramping up |

### 10. Batch / Phase Interface
| Direction | Signal | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Batch → P-1102 | Start / Stop request | From transfer phase [TBC: phase name] |
| Batch → P-1102 | Speed reference | % of max speed [TBC] |
| Batch → P-1102 | Watchdog | Heartbeat |
| P-1102 → Batch | Running / Stopped / Faulted / Interlocked / Mode | |
| P-1102 → Batch | Speed feedback | |
| P-1102 → Batch | Trip reason code | Source Low (I1), Destination High (I2), Discharge High (I3), Instrument Fault (I4), VFD Fault, Feedback Fail |

On a trip, P-1102 stops and reports the reason. Whether the phase holds or aborts is defined in the phase specification [doc ref], not in this narrative.

### 11. HMI
- Standard VFD pump faceplate [name/version]
- The faceplate shows the live state of P4–P7 and I1–I4, plus PT-1102 value, LSL-110 and LSH-120 status, and speed feedback.
- Bypass of P4/I1, if approved, requires [supervisor] security level and is logged in the event journal.

| 2 | Is there a transfer valve path requiring a proven-open permissive (P7)? | Process | Open |

| 7 | Is batch phase end by T-110 level/weight or by LSL-110? | Batch eng. | Open |

FAT: [ ]  SAT: [ ]. Each of P1–P7 and I1–I4 needs a test step, plus the failure cases in Section 8 (wire break on each switch, PT bad quality, batch comms loss, VFD comms loss, power restoration).

## Notes for rolling this out to 120 modules

- **Write the class standards first.** Do one each for VFD pump, on/off valve, modulating valve, and agitator. Most of Sections 3, 4, 8, 10, and 11 will then be "per standard," and each module narrative will be one or two pages of real content.
- **Add a cross-check column.** Add a "Narrative Ref (I#/P#)" column to the alarm database. Every alarm that triggers an interlock should then point to a row in Section 6, and every row in Section 6 should point back. This keeps the spreadsheets and the narratives consistent.
- **Watch the CIP question.** Open Item 3 is the most likely place for a hidden design gap in a food plant. Raise it early and across all transfer pumps, not one pump at a time.
